item.title: Cardinals 'stud' projected to land with Bills, Bengals or Jaguars in blockbuster trade
item.description: Cardinals 'stud' projected to land with Bills, Bengals or Jaguars in blockbuster trade originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Arizona Cardinals aren't having their year, so they're one of the teams being talked about a lot when it comes to potentially making a blockbuster trade before the deadline in November. One Cardinals player is being singled out as a real trade find. This player has been an absolute star for this team, but it may be beneficial to both parties to send him elsewhere. In a feature ahead of the NFL's Week 7 slate of games , Jordan Dajani of CBS Sports names five players he'd "like to see get a change of scenery." He adds that this is more of a wish list of players he'd like to see traded, so it's not like it's definitely happening. Cardinals star Budda Baker could be a trade target before the November deadline Dajani notes that Cardinals safety Budda Baker has been quite a find for the team since they picked him No. 36 overall in the 2017 NFL Draft. He was in the Pro Bowl as a rookie and has been there eight times now. "Not many players have made 1,000 tackles before age 30. Just Bobby Wagner, Roquan Smith, Luke Kuechly, Lavonte David, Ray Lewis, Fred Warner and... Budda Baker," he adds. Dajani calls Baker a "stud," which was shown off during the team's surprising win over the Los Angeles Rams . In that game, he had six tackles, one sack, two tackles for loss and one pass defensed, per Dajani. "He stopped at least one touchdown from being scored, and he was effective in blitzing the quarterback and stopping the running backs. Someone come get him," he adds. Dajani believes the Buffalo Bills , Cincinnati Bengals and Jacksonville Jaguars would be apt fits for Baker. Cardinals fans would hate to see him go, but it would be for the greater good. item.title: Higgins and Lisowski knocked out of NI Open
item.description: Jack Lisowski won his first ranking title at the Northern Ireland Open last year [Getty Images] John Higgins and reigning champion Jack Lisowski became the latest big names to fall at the Northern Ireland Open, but home favourite Jordan Brown progressed to the third round. After an emotional victory in Belfast last year , Lisowski was knocked out in the second round at the Waterfront Hall after losing 4-1 to Anthony McGill. Higgins was another high-profile casualty as he fell to a 4-2 defeat by Wales' Jak Jones, while Stuart Bingham also exited after a 4-0 loss to Ka Wai Cheung. But there was success for Brown, who had beaten friend Mark Allen in an emotional first-round match on Tuesday. On Wednesday, Brown won the final two frames against Michael Holt to prevail 4-3 and set up a third-round encounter with Scott Donaldson. Wales' Mark Williams defeated Zhang Anda 4-2, while there were also wins for Daniel Wells and David Gilbert on Wednesday. item.title: Bayern Munich’s Tom Bischof details Declan Rice battle and speaks on Harry Kane’s tactical role
item.description: Bayern Munich’s Tom Bischof details Declan Rice battle and speaks on Harry Kane’s tactical role Bayern Munich midfielder Tom Bischof reflected on his demanding individual battle with Declan Rice and offered some useful insight into Harry Kane’s unusually deep role following Wednesday evening’s 2-2 Champions League draw with Arsenal. The 21-year-old started alongside Aleksandar Pavlovic in the absence of Joshua Kimmich and found himself confronted with one of European football’s most accomplished midfield units. Bischof nevertheless appeared to relish the challenge of matching up against Rice. “Yeah, that wasn’t just anybody I was playing against,” Bischof said of his duels with the England international in his post-match interview with DAZN . “In my opinion, one has to dig in and get a little pesky, always be present and get on his nerves. Also to be clever and use one’s body cleverly. I know that I’m not the broadest and tallest, but I know how to use my body. In the final analysis, it was a little confusing figuring out who to mark.” Bischof’s continued development in central midfield has already become a significant theme for both club and country this season. Get German Football News recently highlighted his movement and tactical intelligence during Jürgen Klopp’s first Germany victory , while the Bayern youngster himself subsequently declared that he felt well suited to Klopp’s high-intensity national-team approach. Bischof details Arsenal’s difficult rotations The former Hoffenheim talent explained that Arsenal’s constant positional interchanges complicated Bayern’s defensive assignments throughout the evening. “They [Arsenal] did it very well,” Bischof continued. “They had a lot of counter shift movements. [Riccardo] Calafiori also kept making those runs, while [Martin] Ødegaard was moving all over the pitch as well. That naturally wasn’t easy. I still think we did well and could have gotten all three points had we converted more of our chances.” Bayern initially struggled to establish themselves against Arsenal’s possession game before growing into the contest. Alphonso Davies cancelled out Eberechi Eze’s opener before Harry Kane converted a second-half penalty to put Vincent Kompany’s side ahead. Declan Rice ultimately denied Bayern all three points with an 82nd-minute equalizer. Bischof confirms Kane’s deep role was planned Perhaps the most intriguing tactical feature of Bayern’s performance involved Kane. The England captain repeatedly abandoned the conventional centre-forward position to collect possession deep inside his own half. Kane could occasionally be found around Bayern’s defensive midfield line and even took a goal kick during the first half. When former Bayern midfielder Michael Ballack raised Kimmich’s absence during the DAZN interview, Bischof confirmed that Kane’s movements were deliberate rather than an improvised response to Bayern losing their usual midfield organizer. Bischof’s explanation after full-time nevertheless made one aspect clear: Bayern’s increasingly unconventional use of Kane is very much by design. GGFN | Peter Weis

item.title: Luis Díaz forced off in Bayern Munich vs. Arsenal with ‘muscular problems’
item.description: MUNICH, GERMANY - OCTOBER 21: Luis Diaz of FC Bayern Munich looks on before the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between FC Bayern München and Arsenal FC at Football Arena Munich on October 21, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Stuart Franklin - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images) | UEFA via Getty Images Bayern Munich gave a terrific account of itself in a 2-2 Champions League slugfest against Arsenal on Wednesday. However, the Bavarians now have a major concern at the left wing position after Luis Díaz went down late with a non-contact injury. After picking up a knock late in the weekend match against RB Leipzig, Díaz was a precautionary omission from the starting XI, with regular left-back Alphonso Davies in his place at wing. The Colombian international was finally introduced in the 68th minute — and only made it until the 90th before going down on the field away from the ball. “He already had muscular problems before the game and felt it slightly again now,” Bayern board member for sport Max Eberl confirmed after the game in comments captured by Sky Germany reporter Kerry Hau (via @iMiaSanMia ). “We didn’t want to take any risks. Let’s wait and see…” Bayern coach Vincent Kompany struck an upbeat tone. “I don’t think it’s serious. But when it happens twice in a short time, then it’s something to worry about a bit,” Kompany shared . If Díaz is indeed forced to be out for a spell, Davies could see much more time in the Bayern attack in the coming weeks. More to come as soon as we learn more about the injury. item.title: Ballon d’Or 2026 power rankings: Who leads the race with a week until ceremony?
item.description: The race for the Ballon d’Or is entering its final stretch as we enter the final week before the world’s best player is crowned in London. Spain’s triumph over Argentina in the World Cup final will surely bode well for the likes of 2024 winner Rodri and Lamine Yamal in their pursuit of the individual accolade, who have both played their part in Barcelona’s stunning 100 percent start to the new campaign, hoping it will complement their role in winning football’s most coveted trophy. Harry Kane remains the football purist’s favourite for the Ballon d’Or, however, following his sublime goalscoring campaign with Bayern Munich and after making a series of important interventions at the World Cup with England, too. Will it be enough to make team achievements irrelevant come the ceremony on 25 October? During the World Cup, eight-time Ballon d’Or winner Lionel Messi showed that he can still force himself into the conversation at the age of 39, firing eight goals to propel Argentina to the final and briefly take the crown as the competition’s all-time top goalscorer - until he was eclipsed by Kylian Mbappe , while Sir David Beckham has tipped the Argentine to win after inspiring Inter Miami to the Campeones Cup. Here’s how the top 10 front-runners stack up in The Independent’s Ballon d’Or 2026 power rankings: 10. Pau Cubarsi 🆕 What’s this, a new entry to the power rankings?! Barcelona’s Cubarsi is favourite to bring home the Golden Boy award, but he’s so far been bumped from our list by Vinicius Jr, who squeezed into our top 10 mainly to spare myself some angry emails from those affiliated to Real Madrid and Brazil (I joke, kind of). The 2024 runner-up had another strong season at the Bernabeu, netting 22 goals in 36 appearances, though was unable to inspire the club to a trophy. item.title: Lightning beat Golden Knights 6-2 as Kucherov ties franchise points record
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 20: Nikita Kucherov #86 and Emil Lilleberg #78 of the Tampa Bay Lightning celebrate Kucherov’s third-period goal against the Vegas Golden Knights at T-Mobile Arena on October 20, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Lightning defeated the Golden Knights 6-2. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) Getty Images LAS VEGAS (AP) — Anthony Cirelli scored twice, Nikita Kucherov had three points to tie Tampa Bay’s career scoring record, and the Lightning extended their strong start by beating the Vegas Golden Knights 6-2 on Tuesday night. The Lightning (7-2) are off to their best start since opening 7-1-1 in 2020-21, when they repeated as Stanley Cup champions. Vegas had won seven of eight. Kucherov has at least one point in all 15 games he’s played against the Golden Knights. That ranks behind only Mario Lemieux (26 games against Calgary) and Tomas Sandstrom (17 games against Tampa Bay) among players who scored in every game against an opponent. Connor McDavid had a 17-game streak against New Jersey that ended in January. With a goal and two assists, Kucherov increased his total to 1,137 career points, pulling even with former teammate Steven Stamkos for the club record. Brandon Hagel, John Carlson and Victor Hedman also scored for the Lightning. Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 32 shots. Ivan Barbashev scored his first goal of the season for the Golden Knights, and Mark Stone got his fifth in three games. Carter Hart made 15 saves on 21 shots. Cirelli gave Tampa Bay a 3-2 lead 6:44 into the second period off a pass from Kucherov, then scored unassisted to make it 4-2 at 10:09. Both teams played a wide-open game. Each side scored twice in the first period before the Lightning broke it open with three goals in the second for a 5-2 lead. Those five goals came on 14 shots, the last from the left point by Hedman that somehow got by Hart late in the second. Kucherov’s breakaway goal early in the third made it 6-2. Golden Knights forward Brett Howden, drafted 27th overall by the Lightning in 2016, played in his 500th career game. It was his 322nd for Vegas. Up next Lightning: Visit the Colorado Avalanche on Friday. Golden Knights: Visit the St. Louis Blues on Thursday.

item.description: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick at the end of his side's humbling 4-1 loss away to Como in the Champions League on Wednesday (PIERO CRUCIATTI) Manchester United were hammered 4-1 by Como in the Champions League on Wednesday as the pressure increased on beleaguered manager Michael Carrick, while a late Declan Rice equaliser earned Arsenal a 2-2 draw away to Bayern Munich. Elsewhere, Real Madrid thumped RB Leipzig 4-1 and there were also notable victories for Inter Milan, Aston Villa and Real Betis. The most remarkable scoreline, though, came in driving rain on the banks of Lake Como, where United suffered their joint-heaviest loss in the Champions League in the last 30 years. Nico Paz scored twice for Cesc Fabregas's Como, with Tasos Douvikas and Jacobo Ramon getting their other goals. This was a second 4-1 home win in this season's competition for the tournament debutants. Joshua Zirkzee pulled one back at the death for United, but they are now seven games without a win in all competitions. The Red Devils have just one win in the Premier League this season and have now suffered back-to-back losses in Europe. Carrick's position risks becoming untenable. "I have not given my own position any thought," Carrick said. "For us to play in that way, it's not acceptable. It wasn't a good performance at all," he admitted. item.title: Villa tame Viking to stay perfect in Champions League
item.description: Aston Villa midfielder Ross Barkley (left) celebrates his goal against Viking in the Champions League (Henry NICHOLLS) Aston Villa maintained their perfect start to the Champions League on Wednesday, cruising to a 3-1 win against Norwegian side Viking to strengthen their push for a top-eight finish in the league phase. Ross Barkley put the dominant home side ahead midway through the first half and Emiliano Buendia stroked home a penalty to double their lead at Villa Park. An own goal from Henrik Heggheim shortly after the hour mark made the game all but safe for Villa, though the visitors grabbed a late consolation. "We played a very safe match," Villa boss Unai Emery told TNT Sports. "First half we dominated, we were feeling comfortable. "The second half we started not like the first half and conceded some corners. In 90 minutes overall we were better and dominated more than less. "We're so happy how we're getting those three points." Emery's new-look team have now won all of their opening three Champions League matches following a 3-2 victory against Club Brugge and a 6-0 mauling of Fenerbahce. An upturn in fortunes in the Premier League means Villa have now won five out of six games in all competitions -- a dramatic turnaround after a slow start to the season. Viking drew 3-3 with six-time European champions Bayern Munich last week but the home team were dominant from the start on Wednesday. Nicolas Jackson had two free headers, both of which he directed tamely at goalkeeper Arild Ostbo. The opener came in the 23rd minute when midfielder Barkley rose to nod home Ibrahim Mbaye's corner. Villa doubled their lead from the penalty spot in the 37th minute when Zlatko Tripic was penalised for a foul on Alysson after a VAR review. Buendia stepped up and nonchalantly stroked the ball home. The visitors started the second half brightly, forcing Villa back, but Alysson was inches away from extending Villa's lead. And they had a three-goal cushion after Heggheim deflected Alysson's effort into the net following a swift counter-attack. Peter Christiansen gave the away fans something to cheer in the final few minutes with a superb volley following a cross from the right. Victory leaves Villa well placed to finish in the top eight, which would guarantee direct qualification for the last 16 of Europe's top club competition. Villa enjoyed an outstanding 2025/26 season, finishing fourth in the Premier League and winning the Europa League -- their first major trophy for 30 years. Emery was faced with the task of a huge rebuild after a series of high-profile departures during the summer transfer window, including Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa, Emiliano Martinez, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne. But his new side is rapidly taking shape, helped by new signings such as Jackson and Switzerland forward Johan Manzambi, who missed Wednesday's match with an injury. jw/iwd

All five of the highest-graded quarterbacks in PFN’s QB Impact metric entered their current programs from somewhere else, and several have completely changed the trajectory of their careers in the process. Miami’s Darian Mensah leads the group by a substantial margin, but Gio Lopez, Conner Weigman, Aidan Chiles, and Michael Hawkins Jr. have all emerged as major reasons their respective teams have exceeded expectations. PFN college football analyst Max Chadwick broke down the five highest-graded quarterbacks in the country based on PFN Impact. Here is his top five entering the second half of the season. 5) Michael Hawkins Jr., West Virginia PFN QB Impact Grade: 91.6 Michael Hawkins Jr. has found a much better fit at West Virginia than he did earlier in his career at Oklahoma. Hawkins has rushed for 749 yards this season, the most among FBS quarterbacks. His passing production had been much more modest until his breakout against Cincinnati, when he delivered easily the best performance of his career. item.title: Mourinho admits Courtois was crucial as Demichelis sees improvement in his team's performance
item.description: Mourinho admits Courtois was crucial as Demichelis sees improvement in his team's performance José Mourinho was pleased with Real Madrid’s performance against RB Leipzig but was quick to credit goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois for playing a crucial role in the 4-1 Champions League victory. Leipzig created several dangerous opportunities in an entertaining first half, forcing Courtois into important saves. Madrid eventually took the lead through Bernardo Silva shortly before the break before Arda Güler, Kylian Mbappé and Yan Diomande secured the result after half-time. “To be honest, our keeper Courtois was crucial tonight,” Mourinho said. He also praised Leipzig and their goalkeeper Maarten Vandevoordt for their energetic performance, while noting that maintaining such intensity throughout a match of this level is difficult. Madrid took advantage as the game progressed, with Mourinho explaining that his team began to find their rhythm and make their chances count. The victory continued a promising start to the Champions League campaign for the Spanish giants. “I think the way we are playing is positive, and you start getting a positive feeling in this competition as a Real Madrid player and fan. We’ve had a good start to this campaign,” Mourinho added. For Leipzig, the defeat brought further frustration, but headcoach Demichelis insisted that his team had shown considerable improvement following their heavy loss against Bayern Munich. “I have a bad feeling because it was another defeat. But there is also something positive in it because we were significantly better than against Bayern,” the Leipzig coach said. Demichelis felt his side had created enough chances to deserve more from the contest, arguing that going into half-time trailing 1-0 did not reflect the balance of play. He also drew a clear distinction between the two recent defeats. “Against Bayern, we did nothing. A defeat like today’s is something you can accept because you know you gave everything. Against Bayern, we were simply passive. Today, we were active,” he explained. Leipzig will have little time to dwell on the result, with Demichelis already looking ahead to the next fixture and the opportunity to give the club’s supporters something to celebrate. The coach was also delighted to see Christoph Baumgartner return from injury, describing the midfielder as a leader and an important attacking presence. “He deserved to play today against Madrid. We need him, and he is very important for us going forward. We know how good he is and how important he is for us,” Demichelis said. Nevertheless, the Leipzig coach acknowledged that one problem remains unresolved: his team are conceding too many goals. “We have conceded too many goals recently. Naturally, I am not happy with that,” he admitted.

item.title: Lando Norris risks unwanted F1 record as disastrous title defence continues
item.description: Motorsport photo After winning the 2025 Formula 1 championship and forever solidifying his name in the history books, Lando Norris is putting together one of the worst title defences the championship has ever seen. The Briton currently sits sixth in the drivers' standings on just 201 points with six races to go. If he finishes sixth or lower, he will be the first reigning champion to finish outside the top five the following season since Damon Hill in 1997. Hill won the title with Williams in 1996, but was dropped by the team and moved to Arrows, finishing 12th in 1997. Since then, the worst a reigning champion has finished is fifth. 1998: Jacques Villeneuve , Williams, fifth 2009: Lewis Hamilton , McLaren , fifth 2010: Jenson Button , McLaren, fifth 2014: Sebastian Vettel , Red Bull, fifth Arguably, Nico Rosberg failed to defend his title after becoming champion in 2016 due to his retirement, but I'm not sure that counts. Norris is only 14 points behind Ferrari's Charles Leclerc , who sits in fifth, and 20 points behind Max Verstappen in fourth. So even though there are no sprint race weekends left this season, it's still possible for Norris to pull himself out of this slump. But that's if McLaren can improve the car before it's too late. Lando Norris, McLaren Lando Norris, McLaren "The car's not quick enough and it's too difficult to drive. We're a long way off," he told the media after he finished fourth at the Singapore Grand Prix. "You have to always look at the package, you know?" team principal Andrea Stella said. "I think we know that tracks with long straights, we are not that great. The package is not strong in these circuits. "So tracks like Baku, like Monza, like Las Vegas will be difficult. The the car is strong in low speed, in very small tight, little corners when you have to be on brakes... these kind of things. I think it's quite good, but it's not the best so we need to work on that. You know it has strength, it has weaknesses and it will go up and down for the rest of the season." item.title: Arsenal 'concerned' about Saka injury, says Arteta
item.description: Bukayo Saka was subbed out early in Wednesday's match at Bayern (Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND) Arsenal coach Mikel Arteta said the club was "concerned" about the severity of an injury to winger Bakayo Saka after Wednesday's pulsating 2-2 Champions League draw at Bayern Munich. Saka, Arsenal's joint top goalscorer this season alongside Victor Gyokeres, went off early after falling to the turf grabbing his thigh and was replaced by Eberechi Eze. Eze scored Arsenal's opener and Declan Rice scored late to clinch a draw for last season's runners up after an Alphonso Davies goal and a Harry Kane penalty for the hosts. Arteta said Saka's injury was as yet unclear, but told reporters the club's medical staff were worried. "They are a bit concerned about Saka. When a player has to come off with sharp pain it is never good news. We have to wait and see," Arteta said. "The level of intensity this game requires as well is something incredible. You could see it last night, the PSG-Barcelona game. "The level that you need, it's unbelievable. It's the highest level and those things happen, unfortunately. "He doesn't look good at all, but we'll have to wait and see," the Spaniard added. Arteta spoke glowingly of his side's efforts, while praising those of the home side. "Bayern batter every team, so I really value what the boys did tonight," he said. "That's one of the highest levels we have played... The level of opposition and our level as well. It was two teams that wanted to attack and play." Rice was thrilled with his late goal. "I'm so happy. When you play against teams like Bayern that are man-to-man all over the pitch, you have to apply certain principles," Rice told TNT. "I just kept running, lost my marker and I was in on goal to score." dwi/iwd

item.title: I’ve not given my position any thought – Carrick quiet on quit talk
item.description: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick reacts following the UEFA Champions League match between Como 1907 and Manchester United at the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium. (is associated with: «I’ve not given my position any thought – Carrick quiet on quit talk») Luca Rossini/PA Wire/dpa Under-pressure Michael Carrick claims not to have given his position any thought after a humiliating Champions League loss at Como that saw him apologize to Manchester United fans and question his players. An awful start to the season reached a nadir on Wednesday evening in Italy, where the Red Devils’ winless run stretched to a seventh successive match in all competitions for the first time since 2015. Cesc Fàbregas’ Como outplayed United from the outset, with burgeoning star Nico Paz’s brace complemented by Tasos Douvikas and Jacobo Ramon goals before substitute Joshua Zirkzee scored a stoppage-time consolation. Under-fire boss Carrick held his hands up apologetically to the largely empty away end at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia after a damaging 4-1 loss that puts his position in jeopardy. “First of all, I have to apologize to the supporters,” the United boss said. “I went over to the (away) end, and I care about this football club as much as anyone, if not more with the position that I’m in and what I value this football club. “For us to play in that way is not acceptable. It wasn’t a good performance at all. We wanted to build on what we brought to Leeds and the performance that we had at Leeds. “That bit of intensity, that spirit, that aggression, that real willingness to give everything, and tonight was the total opposite of a performance, I have to say. It was tough to watch.” Carrick sidestepped a question about whether he would quit during a press conference that ended with the United boss being asked if he feared he could lose his job. “Listen, I’ve not given my own position any thought,” he said. “It is the supporters (I am thinking about). I was one of them tonight watching that and I wasn’t happy at all.” Carrick’s fury was palpable after a performance that was markedly different from the purposeful draw at Leeds that he felt marked a “fresh start”. Instead, the display and post-match apology was strikingly similar to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s reaction to the 4-1 loss at Watford that proved his final match as United boss in November 2021. “We can all play well, we can all have poor performances,” Carrick, who was part of the Norwegian’s staff, said. “But to do it in that manner is really not right at all. “It wasn’t just the goals, it was the manner and the way we played at times, in the way we went about it, was the difficult thing to watch for me.” Carrick said he hoped United’s players’ lives are “wrapped around the football club” like his is and admitted he found it “difficult to understand how it can be so different” to Sunday’s display at Elland Road. (is associated with: «I’ve not given my position any thought – Carrick quiet on quit talk») Luca Rossini/PA Wire/dpa Under-pressure Michael Carrick claims not to have given his position any thought after a humiliating Champions League loss at Como that saw him apologize to Manchester United fans and question his players. An awful start to the season reached a nadir on Wednesday evening in Italy, where the Red Devils’ winless run stretched to a seventh successive match in all competitions for the first time since 2015. Cesc Fàbregas’ Como outplayed United from the outset, with burgeoning star Nico Paz’s brace complemented by Tasos Douvikas and Jacobo Ramon goals before substitute Joshua Zirkzee scored a stoppage-time consolation. Under-fire boss Carrick held his hands up apologetically to the largely empty away end at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia after a damaging 4-1 loss that puts his position in jeopardy. “First of all, I have to apologize to the supporters,” the United boss said. “I went over to the (away) end, and I care about this football club as much as anyone, if not more with the position that I’m in and what I value this football club. “For us to play in that way is not acceptable. It wasn’t a good performance at all. We wanted to build on what we brought to Leeds and the performance that we had at Leeds. “That bit of intensity, that spirit, that aggression, that real willingness to give everything, and tonight was the total opposite of a performance, I have to say. It was tough to watch.” Carrick sidestepped a question about whether he would quit during a press conference that ended with the United boss being asked if he feared he could lose his job. “Listen, I’ve not given my own position any thought,” he said. “It is the supporters (I am thinking about). I was one of them tonight watching that and I wasn’t happy at all.” Carrick’s fury was palpable after a performance that was markedly different from the purposeful draw at Leeds that he felt marked a “fresh start”. Instead, the display and post-match apology was strikingly similar to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s reaction to the 4-1 loss at Watford that proved his final match as United boss in November 2021. “We can all play well, we can all have poor performances,” Carrick, who was part of the Norwegian’s staff, said. “But to do it in that manner is really not right at all. “It wasn’t just the goals, it was the manner and the way we played at times, in the way we went about it, was the difficult thing to watch for me.” Carrick said he hoped United’s players’ lives are “wrapped around the football club” like his is and admitted he found it “difficult to understand how it can be so different” to Sunday’s display at Elland Road. It compares even more starkly to the start of a year that saw the Red Devils earn a Champions League return, Carrick the permanent post and Bruno Fernandes player of the year honours. The United skipper has been a pale imitation of that performer this term and questioned Carrick’s tactics as another Champions League trip ended in an eye-catching post-match player interview. Lisandro Martínez lashed out at the club hierarchy after last week’s loss at Atlético Madrid and this time Fernandes said it was the staff’s decision at Como “not to press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little bit of space in behind”. “We actually half-pressed man-to-man in the second half and then conceded a goal from that,” Carrick said in response. “And there’s a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don’t run, and you don’t run forward, and you don’t run back, you aren’t going to win.”

The England star lasted just 10 minutes at the Allianz Arena before going down in agony after playing what appeared to be a routine pass, raising his arm to signal he required medical attention. The 25-year-old was also seen grabbing at his thigh as medical personnel rushed onto the pitch to tend to him. -Credit:Christina Pahnke - sampics, Getty Images Saka's night was over right then and there, with Eberechi Eze coming on as his replacement for the remainder of the contest. Following the match, which concluded in a 2-2 draw courtesy of goals from Eze, Alphonso Davies, Harry Kane and Declan Rice, Arteta provided an update on Saka's condition. He said, via football.london : "They are a bit concerned. A player who has to come off with a really sharp pain is never good news, but we'll have to wait and see." Any significant spell on the sidelines would represent a substantial setback for the defending Premier League champions, given the enormous influence Saka carries in every game he plays. When factored in alongside the existing injury concerns within Arteta's first-team squad, the situation could rapidly develop into a serious problem for the North London club. item.title: Kings pick up long-awaited first win of season with their best offensive output so far
item.description: WASHINGTON, DC - OCTOBER 20: Alex Laferriere #14 of the Los Angeles Kings skates against the Washington Capitals during the third period at Capital One Arena on October 20, 2026 in Washington, DC. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) Getty Images WASHINGTON (AP) — Through their first six games, the Los Angeles Kings had scored a league-worst 12 goals. As a result, they were the NHL’s sole winless team entering Tuesday night. But the Kings’ offense made a late push at the end of the first period against Washington, and that propelled Los Angeles to a 5-2 win over the Capitals. “Obviously it was a tough start, and the longer it goes, the more you feel that pressure to get one,” said goalie Darcy Kuemper, who made 30 saves. “But I think going into the third in the tie game, we just talked amongst ourselves and said, ‘Everyone’s going to dig down, we’re going to get this job done.’ So it was a big win for us.” Los Angeles (1-6-2) was down 2-0 in the first period but tied it in a span of 31 seconds with goals by Adrian Kempe and Artemi Panarin. “Obviously it’s hard to play with a lot of confidence when you haven’t won a game,” Kempe said. “Seeing the pucks go in, I think helped everybody a lot.” The Kings had scored just four goals over their past four games. They exceeded that total against Washington and had their highest-scoring game of the season thanks to Scott Laughton’s late empty-netter. Erik Gustafsson made it 3-2 in the third period, and Kempe gave LA a two-goal advantage with his second of the game. Los Angeles lost center Quinton Byfield in the first to an upper-body injury that coach Peter Laviolette said would be evaluated Wednesday. “To be down 2-0, it would’ve been easy for us to kind of put our heads down and say, ‘Here we go again. Another one getting away from us,’” Kuemper said. “But instead we got huge response by those guys. What a shift to get two goals to finish the period. And then you feel like you’re right back in the game and feel like you have a chance. And like I said, we wanted to get that monkey off our back and you could see everyone bear down and get the job done.” It was Laviolette’s first win of his seventh stint as an NHL head coach. “Everybody’s happy,” he said. “I mean the guys have been working hard.” Now that the pressure is off, the Kings hope they can settle into the season. “I don’t think it’s unusual for teams to go on losing streaks throughout the year, but when it’s at the start of the year, it gets magnified and it feels a lot worse for us,” Kuemper said. “It looks a lot worse. So nice to get a win and now we just got to get rolling.”

We're still in a performance business where the only thing that matters to the people upstairs sometimes is how you are playing. Players get lost in that, and we don't feel human sometimes, because we're not viewed as human. We’re viewed as gladiators who just need to go perform and be entertainers for the fans on Sunday. “But the reality is we are human beings. item.title: Japan is known for world-class events - but the Asian Games were chaotic
item.description: [Getty Images] From the Olympics to Tokyo's annual video game convention, Japan has a strong track record of hosting major international events. But this year's Asian Games in Nagoya and the wider Aichi Prefecture were marred by problems. There were diplomatic blunders, transport errors and accommodation chaos. In comment fields online, some branded it the "worst Games in history" and urged a "full investigation". Prof Kozo Tomiyama, who studies major sporting events at Osaka University, believes organisers were unable to handle the unexpected. "If these problems damage international confidence in Japan's ability to operate sporting events, they could also affect Japan's ability to attract international competitions in the future," he warned. The deputy director general of the Games, Takaaki Omi, admitted organisers had faced a range of unforeseen issues, but insisted they took on feedback and made improvements. String of incidents Before the tournament had even begun, participants were complaining about too few rooms and poor-quality accommodation. Organisers had decided to forgo building a traditional athletes' village to cut costs, and were instead housing participants in hotels and container-style units across Nagoya. A top Korean basketball official said tall athletes housed in the containers were struggling to "stretch their legs out on the beds" . Last-minute additions to the total number of participants strained the city's capacity so much that an Italian cruise ship with 1,500 cabins was used to fill the gap. The organising committee had initially arranged accommodation for up to 15,000 delegation members "in accordance with the host city contract", Omi told the BBC. But as other sports were added, the number grew by 2,000 to a total of 17,000 . Organisers initially claimed there was "simply nowhere" to put up the late influx and told them to make their own arrangements - before backpedalling and releasing a joint statement with the Olympic Council of Asia promising that all "17,000-plus" guests would get "Games-appropriate accommodation". Container units were used to host some participants as organisers opted not to build a traditional athletes' village [Getty Images] This was just the start of the problems. Over the course of the Games, athletes were bussed to the wrong venues and the North Korean anthem was played for the South Korean men's hockey team . During the men's football gold medal ceremony, the South Korean flag was not raised properly. Taiwan's sports minister found himself temporarily barred from a flag-raising event. In the last days of the Games, volunteers received an email inviting them to the closing ceremony free of charge. But later an organiser said the decision to distribute free tickets was still under review and had not been approved. Omi admitted the string of incidents at the event - which was bigger than the Paris Olympics by number of participants - had caused significant inconvenience for some delegations.

Last week the Tokyo Shimbun newspaper accused the firm of aggressively cutting corners on hiring, resulting in a shortage of experienced staff capable of managing the issues which arose. Officials ended up having to send a formal apology to South Korea for the series of mishaps affecting that particular delegation. Glitches have continued at the ongoing Para Games, where the wrong national anthems were played at three events. Nagoya Mayor Ichiro Hirosawa, who is also deputy head of the Games organising committee, called it "unacceptable" and offered his apologies. Prof Tomiyama hopes organisers will take lessons from the past few weeks to deliver higher-quality sporting events in the future. item.description: Source: T.Schneider/Depositphotos LIV Golf’s fight to secure its future has opened another front in professional golf’s ongoing division. The breakaway league has accused the DP World Tour of interfering with its efforts to recruit players for a proposed restructuring. The accusation surfaced during bankruptcy proceedings in the United States, where LIV is working toward a new business model and trying to retain players. The dispute intensified after the European-based circuit announced restrictions affecting golfers who join LIV’s planned 2027 operation. With several prominent players reconsidering their commitments, the clash has added another complication to an already uncertain transition for the league. LIV Golf challenges the DP World Tour’s new restrictions During a bankruptcy court hearing on October 14, LIV Golf attorney Rob Fitzgerald criticized the DP World Tour’s decision to prevent golfers joining the proposed LIV 2.0 from holding membership on the European circuit in 2027. According to Golf Digest, LIV’s legal team described the move as an attempt to interfere with the league’s recruitment process. Fitzgerald’s objection came as LIV worked to persuade players to commit to its proposed next phase. The accusation reflects a growing conflict over whether golfers can retain access to established tours while joining a league undergoing major financial and organizational changes. The DP World Tour announced its position on October 12, making clear that players intending to compete in LIV Golf 2.0 would not be offered membership for the 2027 season. item.title: Indiana QB Josh Hoover struggled vs. Michigan DC Jay Hill’s BYU defense last year
item.description: PROVO, UT - NOVEMBER 15: Josh Hoover #10 of the Texas Christian University Horned Frogs escapes pressure from Viliami Po'uha #45 of the Brigham Young Cougars during the first half of their game at LaVell Edwards Stadium on November 15, 2025 in Provo, Utah. (Photo by Chris Gardner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Could past be prologue when it comes to how Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover performs versus a defense coached by Michigan defensive coordinator Jay Hill? That will certainly be the hope for the Wolverines on Saturday when they take on No. 6 Indiana. Hoover was the quarterback at TCU last season and Hill was the defensive coordinator of BYU. Hill’s defense absolutely took it to Hoover and TCU. In a 44-13 loss to BYU last season, Hoover was 10-of-23 for 183 yards with two interceptions. Hoover was pressured constantly and did not fare well with a heavy pass rush and was sacked four times in all. Josh Hoover’s last outing vs Jay Hill defense: 😬10/23 😬2 INT 😬43.2 QBR 😬L pic.twitter.com/SQFvKNsFWh — Marty McRide (@MartyMcRide) October 19, 2026 Hoover’s had a great start to the 2026 season with Indiana, throwing for 18 touchdowns and zero interceptions. Turnovers were a knock on Hoover when he transferred to the Hoosiers after throwing 13 interceptions last season, but Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti seems to be getting the best out of him, just like he did with Fernando Mendoza. Hoover struggled last week against Ohio State’s relentless pressure and had his worst game of the season in a 19-15 loss, going 20-of-40 for 296 yards and a touchdown. Hoover wasn’t much better in a 20-17 win over Nebraska the week prior, going 12-of-22 for 263 yards and two touchdowns. If Michigan is able to create situations where Hoover is under duress, he could have his third game in a row where his completion rate is hovering around 50%. Michigan’s defense is currently ranked No. 4 in the nation in total defense, No. 13 in passing yards allowed, and No. 33 in team sacks. Michigan’s defense, along with Hill’s scheme and familiarity with Hoover are all advantages for the Wolverines. Whether that correlates in Hoover struggling against Hill’s unit once again remains to be seen, but there’s a strong case that Hoover will have a long day against Michigan and it’ll be the Wolverines pulling off an upset on Saturday.

Hoover was pressured constantly and did not fare well with a heavy pass rush and was sacked four times in all. Josh Hoover’s last outing vs Jay Hill defense: 😬10/23 😬2 INT 😬43.2 QBR 😬L pic.twitter.com/SQFvKNsFWh — Marty McRide (@MartyMcRide) October 19, 2026 Hoover’s had a great start to the 2026 season with Indiana, throwing for 18 touchdowns and zero interceptions. Hoover struggled last week against Ohio State’s relentless pressure and had his worst game of the season in a 19-15 loss, going 20-of-40 for 296 yards and a touchdown. Hoover wasn’t much better in a 20-17 win over Nebraska the week prior, going 12-of-22 for 263 yards and two touchdowns. If Michigan is able to create situations where Hoover is under duress, he could have his third game in a row where his completion rate is hovering around 50%. Michigan’s defense is currently ranked No. 4 in the nation in total defense, No. 13 in passing yards allowed, and No. 33 in team sacks. Michigan’s defense, along with Hill’s scheme and familiarity with Hoover are all advantages for the Wolverines. Whether that correlates in Hoover struggling against Hill’s unit once again remains to be seen, but there’s a strong case that Hoover will have a long day against Michigan and it’ll be the Wolverines pulling off an upset on Saturday.

The release does not say what Kemea or Hutten Metaal will do next, who will run the team, or how the European classes will be organised. The missing rung Yamaha’s last reset, for the 2024 season, was built around a ladder. As the 2024 announcement laid out, Corvers’ Genk-based operation became the Monster Energy Yamaha Factory MXGP team, and Hutten Metaal’s EMX250 squad was promoted into the Factory MX2 team. Yamaha’s off-road racing manager framed it as a system that promotes success to the next level of the Yamaha pyramid. The proof was in the MX2 line-up: Thibault Benistant and Rick Elzinga, both EMX250 champions (2020 and 2022), were retained, and 2023 EMX250 champion Andrea Bonacorsi joined them. The ladder was not new in 2024. Yamaha’s 2019 announcement , made at Imola ahead of the 2020 season, described the official EMX125 and EMX250 teams as the step feeding the factory MX2 and MXGP teams, with the bLU cRU programme below them. With factory MX2 now closed, the next rung above the EMX250 title no longer exists inside Yamaha. Jago Geerts on a Yamaha at the same 2022 round in Spain. Photo: Vanbasten 23 / Wikimedia Commons , CC BY-SA 4.0 Analysis, not announcement: there are three plausible outcomes. Yamaha could keep a restructured EMX250 effort as a development step and send its best riders straight to the 450, skipping the 250 world championship entirely, which is a big jump for a young rider. It could let champions walk to rivals that still run factory MX2 teams. Or it could treat the closure as a pause and bring MX2 back under the new in-house structure once the MXGP team is stable. Yamaha’s wording (restructuring, not closing, the European classes) leaves all three open. Nothing in the release picks one. The competitive context matters too. Triumph took the 2026 MX2 manufacturers’ title , and the 250 class is not short of manufacturers investing. A Yamaha that leaves that fight is a Yamaha that has to be right about the 450. The clock: 137 days to Almonte Yamaha announced on Wednesday, October 14. The provisional 2027 calendar opens on Sunday, February 28 in Andalucia, runs to Bariloche, Argentina on March 14, then goes to Italy for Montevarchi (March 28) and Riola Sardo (April 4), before Spain’s second round (April 18, now the MXGP of Extremadura at Mérida, per the calendar update ) and Pietramurata (April 25). Of the first six rounds, three are in Italy, the base Yamaha has just chosen for its new factory operation. For a team that will be weeks old, that’s a real break. The Argentina round, two weeks after the opener, is the opposite: a long-haul freight and staffing test for a team that will be weeks old. The calendar is provisional, and none of this means Yamaha will struggle. But a new management structure, a new facility and a new roster have to be ready for a season that starts on a fixed date. Yamaha has not said when it will name them. The seats Yamaha’s 2026 MXGP pair was Tim Gajser and Maxime Renaux. Gajser finished third in the final MXGP standings with 659 points; Renaux was eighth with 449. Yamaha was fourth in the manufacturers’ table (794) behind Honda (1,063), KTM (893) and Kawasaki (834). The stated goal of returning to the top step of the podium has a gap to close. The release names no riders for 2027, and Backfire is treating paddock talk about who goes where as unconfirmed until a team or rider announces it. What can be said is that Yamaha is not alone in resetting: Red Bull KTM Factory Racing has also announced that Stefan Simpson replaces Joel Smets as team manager for 2027, with the roster to follow . Two factories with open line-ups and fixed start dates means the rider market, not the technical department, probably sets the first headlines of the winter. Scenarios to watch (all conditional) Fast and lean: Yamaha names a manager and two MXGP riders early and runs a conventional season. This is the lowest-risk outcome and depends on staffing being settled well before February. Visible friction: late announcements and thin staffing show up at the early flyaway or Italian rounds. Yamaha has run its MXGP team through outside operators in the structures described in its 2019 and 2024 announcements, so this is new ground. In-housing is a trend (Opel will run its own Formula E team ), not a guarantee. Talent leakage: EMX250 riders developed under Yamaha sign with manufacturers that still have factory MX2 seats, and Yamaha pays to train the field. MX2 return: after the MXGP team stabilises, Yamaha restores a factory 250 effort, this time on its own terms. Nothing announced supports this, and it should be read as a possibility only. What to watch next Four announcements would answer most of these questions: the name of the MXGP team manager, the 2027 rider line-up, the new structure for EMX250 and EMX125, and the 2027 entry lists. None has a published date. The first hard deadline is the one already on the calendar: February 28 at Almonte. If Yamaha hits it with a full team, this will look like an overdue consolidation. If it does not, the question will be why the announcement came before the plan. If you’re the 2027 EMX250 champion, do you jump straight to a Yamaha 450, or sign with a brand that still has a factory MX2 seat? Tell us in the comments. To a coach who called for versatility from all of his wingers this summer, here was a significant step forward among many from the 18-year-old at Anfield. There were questions over how Ngumoha would adapt to playing on the right even before Liverpool increased the likelihood by signing Bradley Barcola for £123m from Paris Saint-Germain. On his fifth start under Iraola on Tuesday, which his side won 4-3 , Liverpool witnessed an answer: quickly, incisively and confidently. The teenager’s willingness to cut inside from the right and shoot from distance with his left foot captured Iraola’s imagination as much as the devastating run that created Alexis Mac Allister’s second goal of the game. Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.” Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.description: Phil Foden shouted the loudest on a quiet night at the Etihad Stadium, announcing his personal return to form with an instinctive hat-trick as Manchester City dispatched AEK Athens with little fuss. Those in attendance, officially 40,042 but that felt optimistic, saw Foden shine on the right wing and as a central striker, showing there is life without Erling Haaland, who watched from the bench. Admittedly, the opposition were not a match for the Premier League side, whose other goals came from Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki. Stavros Pilios’s consolation was more a reward for the boisterous fans in yellow and black, who created the atmosphere, than for the overall efforts of the visitors. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Kulusevski and Maddison return to form but are Tottenham also back?
item.description: As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry , a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
